title: Reversibility and frequency reduction in periodic and random positive systems
shortTitle: When can faster environmental change help a spread-out population? Exactly when migration circulates
oneLine: For a population spread over patches with fixed migration, making periodic environmental change faster can never raise the long-run growth rate exactly when migration satisfies detailed balance; any circulating migration admits a weak environment where an intermediate speed is best, and for reversible migration random switching strictly lowers growth, proving a 2025 conjecture.
abstract: In the linear patch model x′ = [Q + diag r(ωt)]x a fixed irreducible migration generator Q couples patches whose growth rates r_i vary in time. Does faster environmental change always lower the long-run growth rate? For periodic environments the boundary is exactly detailed balance (no net circulation around any loop of patches; every two-patch system qualifies): reversible migration gives a growth rate that never increases with frequency, strictly decreasing unless r_i(t) = a_i + b(t), while every irreversible Q admits weak rotating environments on two patches with an interior frequency optimum. An explicit certificate d_ij = π_i(C²)_ij − π_j(C²)_ji, computed from Q alone through the group inverse C of −Q, says which two patches to force and in which phase order, with an explicit frequency and a gain bound of order ε² at amplitude ε. This settles the monotonicity conjecture of Benaïm, Lobry, Sari and Strickler for a fixed migration matrix. For reversible migration the quenched Lyapunov exponent under an irreducible finite-state Markov environment strictly decreases with switching speed unless the frozen matrices share a Perron vector, proving Conjecture 1 of Monmarché, Schreiber and Strickler (2025); with a reversible environmental chain the annealed exponent is convex and strictly decreasing. Time-symmetric two-state environments give witnesses according to the sign of an explicit quadratic form, and the classification extends to elliptic diffusions on closed manifolds. The symmetric sufficiency direction and the slow and fast expansions are known; the converse, the certificate, the random strictness and the diffusion converse are the proposed contribution. The guaranteed effects are small at weak amplitude and the classification is existential. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Periodic classification (Theorem A / Theorem 4.1, proof): for an irreducible generator Q, detailed balance ⇔ the principal Floquet growth rate is nonincreasing in frequency for every bounded periodic environment ⇔ the certificate d_ij = π_i(C²)_ij − π_j(C²)_ji vanishes; reversible Q give strict decrease unless r_i(θ) = a_i + b(θ). Hence the Benaïm–Lobry–Sari–Strickler conjecture holds for a fixed migration matrix exactly when it is diagonally symmetrisable (Corollary 4.4).

Weak witnesses (Theorem B / Theorem 5.2, Proposition 5.3, Corollary 5.4, proof): if d_ij ≠ 0, the rotating environment ε(e_i cos θ + ς e_j sin θ) with ς = −sign d_ij has an interior global frequency maximum for all small ε, with gain at least ε²|d_ij|²γ³/(16ζ_ij) at ω* = |d_ij|γ³/(2ζ_ij); periodic switching among finitely many constant environments also works. For the directed three-cycle, ω* = 27/64, g* = 3/256 and ε* = 2187/6487040 (exact).

Random environments (Theorem C / Theorems 7.2–7.4, Proposition 7.6, proof): with reversible migration the quenched Lyapunov exponent is nonincreasing in switching speed for every stationary ergodic environment, and strictly decreasing for finite-state Markov switching unless the frozen matrices share a positive eigenvector — Conjecture 1 of Monmarché, Schreiber and Strickler; irreversible Q has a cyclic Markov counterexample; with a reversible environmental chain the annealed exponent is convex and strictly decreasing.

Two-state environments (Theorem D / Theorem 6.1, proof): time-symmetric two-state witnesses exist when Φ_Q(x) = xᵀΠC²x is negative for some centred x, and not in the slow small-amplitude regime when it is positive definite; for the three-cycle with one fast edge Φ is indefinite and forcing a single patch is a witness.

Elliptic diffusions (Theorem E / Theorem 8.1, Theorem B.1, proof): on a closed manifold, detailed balance of a smooth uniformly elliptic operator is equivalent to frequency monotonicity for every smooth periodic potential, and to time-reversal invariance of growth at one frequency; reversible diffusions with Markov-switching potentials have strictly decreasing quenched exponents.

narration: When can faster environmental change help a spread-out population? An Evidence Press briefing. Picture a population living in several patches of habitat. Individuals move between patches at fixed rates, while the growth rate in each patch rises and falls with the seasons. Ecologists have long asked whether speeding up those environmental swings always lowers the population's long-run growth. For symmetric movement the answer was known to be yes. But a 2025 example with three patches in a one-way loop showed that an intermediate speed can sometimes be best. This paper finds the exact dividing line. Faster periodic change can never raise long-run growth exactly when migration satisfies a condition called detailed balance, meaning there is no net circulation of movement around any loop of patches. Every two-patch system qualifies. If movement does circulate, then some gentle environment, varying just two patches a quarter of a cycle apart, makes an intermediate speed best. A simple certificate computed from the migration rates alone says which two patches to choose and in which order. For balanced migration the same holds when the environment switches at random: faster switching strictly lowers growth, unless switching cannot matter at all. This proves a 2025 conjecture by Monmarché, Schreiber and Strickler. The paper also treats environments that simply alternate between two states, and continuous habitats. The proofs are written out in full, and a script checks every exact constant. The gains from circulation are small for gentle environments, and the result says that a helpful environment exists, not how a particular one behaves. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. Published on the third of November twenty twenty-six, its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.

decisionObject.description: Whether faster environmental change can raise the long-run growth rate of a patch population with fixed migration: never, exactly under detailed balance, with an explicit certificate d_ij from the migration matrix that names a two-patch forcing with an interior frequency optimum otherwise; strict decrease for random Markov switching under reversible migration.
decisionObject.scope: Linear patch models with fixed irreducible migration and periodic or stationary random growth rates, and elliptic diffusions on closed manifolds. Converse witnesses are perturbative; finite-amplitude behaviour, the shape of a given curve, bounded domains and time-varying migration are not settled.
